data.name: HooksChainBlocked
data.value: Nothing was installed: '{0}' is a hook LocalAi did not write, and '{1}' beside it already holds one saved earlier. The first cannot be saved without overwriting the second. Keep whichever of the two should run, remove the other, and run this again: localai hooks install
data.comment: {0} is the hook itself, which the old message never named; {1} is the backup beside it. Naming both is what makes the instruction actionable: only the reader knows which of the two should run.

data.name: HooksChained
data.value: Hooks that were already here were kept, are called first, and a non-zero exit from one of them stops the chain. Moved aside with the suffix {0}: {1}
data.comment: New: hooks install moved the reader's own files aside and said nothing about it. Both languages come from the paragraph in docs/overview.md that already describes chaining, so the tool and the documentation cannot drift apart. {0} is GitHookLayout.ChainedSuffix rather than a copy of it.

data.name: HooksExcluded
data.value: The repository points core.hooksPath into its working tree, so the dispatchers were also added to .git/info/exclude and stay out of git status.
data.comment: The last clause is new: without it the line reports an edit to a file in the reader's repository and never says why. core.hooksPath, the path and git status are a config key, a path and a command: Latin in both.

data.name: HooksInstalled

data.value: LocalAi hooks need LOCALAI_LAUNCHER_PATH, which the stable launcher sets. Run this through the launcher rather than a binary inside a version directory.
data.comment: Not LauncherMissing: that one is about a file that is not there and is printed by doctor. This is about a variable that was never set, and its fix is how the command was invoked. launcher stays Latin and indeclinable, as in the documentation.

data.name: JsonNotSupported
data.value: --json is not available here. The usage marks the commands that take it with [--json].
data.comment: No echo of what was typed. Naming the command meant naming a prefix of it — `hooks` for `hooks install`, because the path is matched against the commands that fill an envelope and an unmatched one is known only by its first word. A prefix names a command the reader did not run. The envelope's own `command` field keeps that first word for correlation; this sentence does not repeat it.

data.name: PolicyUsage
data.value:
Usage: localai policy show localai policy set --residency <RequireFullVram|AllowPartialOffload|AllowCpu> localai policy set --idle-model-keep-alive-seconds <non-negative integer> localai policy set --update-check <on|off> localai policy set --update-check-interval-hours <{0}..{1}> localai policy set --language <en|ru|system>
RequireFullVram Models must sit entirely in video memory. Default. AllowPartialOffload Part of a model may spill to system memory. Requires an adapter that holds at least some of it. Slower. AllowCpu Models may run entirely on the CPU. Works without a usable adapter; substantially slower. Idle keep-alive Seconds to keep an idle model loaded. Zero unloads it immediately and is the default. Update check Whether this installation may ask GitHub if a newer release exists. Off by default; nothing is ever downloaded or installed without you asking. Language What the CLI and the MCP tools answer in. Follows this computer by default, and falls back to English where there is no translation. Commands and option names are never translated.
data.comment: Usage: and every syntax line are byte-identical in both languages. The description column is 23; a Russian caption longer than 19 characters moves it for all six rows.

data.name: PositionNotFromOne
data.value: invalid_position: lines and columns are counted from 1; got line {0}, column {1}.
data.comment: Word for word CodeSearchText.PositionNotFromOne, deliberately duplicated: this CLI is what the instruction block offers when that MCP server is unreachable, and the block quotes the sentence as a literal. LocalAi.Cli does not reference CodeSearch.Mcp, so the two cannot share one resource; a test compares them.

data.name: UpdateCancelled
data.value: Update cancelled. The installed version was not changed.
data.comment: Deliberately narrow: a version directory may already have been published, and only the installed version is claimed unchanged.

data.name: UpdateCheckDisabled
data.value: check disabled; run `localai policy set --update-check on` to look for releases

data.name: UpdateClientsPickItUp
data.value: Anything running out of the previous version was stopped and not restarted; clients start the new one the next time they use a tool.
data.comment: The old wording said nothing was restarted without saying it was stopped, which contradicted this command's own refusal message.

data.name: UpdateDidNotComplete
data.value: Update did not complete: {0}. {1}
data.comment: 0 is a LocalAiPackageInstallStatus enum name and stays Latin; 1 is an English literal from the installer core.

data.name: UpdateFailed
data.value: Update failed: {0}

data.name: UpdateIncomparable
data.value: latest verified release is {0}; this installation does not record which release it came from, so the two cannot be compared. The next install or update records it.

data.name: UpdateInstalled
data.value: Installed LocalAi {0} at {1}.
data.comment: 0 is the release version, not the version directory: the old code passed a commit id where the run had just announced a release number.

data.name: UpdateLookingForRelease
data.value: Looking for the newest release on GitHub...

data.name: UpdateNeverChecked
data.value: unknown; nothing has been checked yet

data.name: UpdateNoInstallation
data.value: There is no LocalAi installation at {0} to update. Run the installer to set one up.

data.name: UpdateNothingToInstall
data.value: Nothing to install: {0} is the newest release, and this installation is not behind it.
data.comment: The old wording named the installation twice with two different identifiers, because DisplayName falls back to a version directory when no release version was recorded.

data.name: UpdateQueueBusy
data.value: The broker has {0} queued job(s). Updating now would stop the tools running them. Run `localai update --wait` to update once they finish.
data.comment: Noun-first in Russian: genitive plural is correct for every count.

data.name: UpdateQueueStillBusy
data.value: Still {0} queued job(s) after {1} minutes. Nothing was changed; try again when the queue is quieter.
data.comment: The Russian reorders the holes, which indexed string.Format allows: it is the only way to avoid opening on a numeral.

data.name: UpdateQueueWaiting
data.value: Waiting for {0} queued job(s) to finish...

data.name: UpdateUnknownOption
data.value: Unknown option '{0}'.

data.name: UpdateUnknownUnavailable
data.value: unknown; the last check produced nothing to believe (tried {0} UTC)

data.name: UpdateUpToDate
data.value: up to date at {0} (checked {1} UTC)

data.name: UpdateUsage
data.value:
Usage: localai update [--wait] [--force]
Installs the newest signed release over this one. The manifest is verified against the embedded release key before the package is downloaded, the package against the manifest before anything is extracted, and the version pointer is swapped atomically once both check out.
--wait Wait up to {0} minutes for queued broker jobs to finish instead of refusing. --force Install the newest release even when it is not newer than this one.
Prerequisites, models and client integrations are not touched; run the installer for those.
data.comment: Usage: and both option names are byte-identical in both languages. The wait ceiling is a hole fed from MaximumWait so the block cannot name a limit the code does not enforce.

data.name: UpdateVerifiedRelease
data.value: {0} (checked {1} UTC)
data.comment: 1 arrives already formatted invariantly.

data.name: VersionComplete
data.value: {0}, all {1} binaries present

data.name: VersionDirectoryMissing
data.value: The pointer names {0} and that directory does not exist.

data.name: VersionFilesMissing
data.value: {0} is missing: {1}

data.name: VersionNoPointer
data.value: No current.json under {0}. Nothing is installed here.

data.name: VersionPointerEmpty
data.value: current.json names no version.

data.name: VersionPointerUnreadable
data.value: current.json cannot be read: {0}
data.comment: 0 is a .NET runtime message and arrives in whatever language the framework speaks.

data.name: WorktreeGone
data.value: Worktree {0} no longer exists; skipping its overlay.
data.comment: worktree and overlay stay Latin and indeclinable: they name a git command and a file on disk the reader would look for.

data.name: WorktreeNotInspectable
data.value: Worktree {0} could not be inspected ({1}); leaving overlays alone this pass.
data.comment: 1 is a .NET runtime message and arrives in whatever language the framework speaks.

data.name: WorktreeVanished
data.value: Worktree {0} disappeared while it was being inspected; skipping its overlay.
data.comment: Kept apart from WorktreeGone on purpose: one is a stale listing, the other a race during the run, and the exception filter exists to tell them apart.
